transcript_excerpt:
Vet: Hi, this must be Biscuit. What brings you in today?
Owner: He's been shaking his head and scratching his left ear for about three weeks.
Vet: His temperature is 101.6, he weighs 34.2 kilograms. The left canal is red with dark waxy discharge. Cytology shows lots of yeast.
Vet: I'll dispense an ear ointment, one pump in each ear twice a day for fourteen days, and carprofen for pain. Let's recheck in two weeks.

1. Record ONLY information that is stated or clearly implied in the transcript or in the supplied patient block. Never invent, infer or "complete" history, examination findings, vital signs, diagnoses, drug names, doses, frequencies, durations or dates.
2. Never fabricate a normal finding. The only permitted exception is a section whose missing_behavior is "use_normal_defaults": there, anything NOT mentioned may be filled with that section's normal_defaults text, and you must set used_defaults to true for that section. Any abnormal finding that IS mentioned always overrides the defaults.
3. Preserve numbers and units exactly as spoken (kg, lb, C, F, mg, mL, mg/kg, bpm, breaths/min). Do not convert units. If a unit is missing or a figure sounds implausible, record what was said and add an entry to review_flags.
4. Distinguish what the owner reported (history) from what the clinician observed or measured (findings), and keep diagnoses ("differential", "suspect", "confirmed") as qualified as the clinician stated them. Do not upgrade a suspicion to a diagnosis.
5. Drug orders: record drug, dose, route, frequency and duration only if each was stated. If any element is missing, garbled or ambiguous, record what is known and add a review_flags entry such as "Carprofen dose not stated - confirm mg/kg". Never calculate a dose yourself.
6. If speakers, the patient, or a fact are unclear (for example speech-to-text errors, conflicting statements, or a pronoun with an unclear referent), do not guess: flag it in review_flags.
7. Put every follow-up, recheck, diagnostic to be run, owner instruction and task for staff in action_items, one short imperative item each. Only include items actually discussed.
8. review_flags are for the clinician: unclear doses, contradictions, missing but clinically important information the template asked for, possible transcription errors, and any default-filled sections that need confirmation. Do not use review_flags for general advice.

<template>
<name>SOAP - General Consult</name>
<appointment_type>general</appointment_type>
<style tone="clinical" use_abbreviations="true">
<custom_instructions>Keep the note concise and scannable; one idea per sentence.</custom_instructions>
</style>
<section id="subjective" title="Subjective" format="paragraph" required="true" missing_behavior="state_not_discussed">
<instructions>Presenting complaint and history as reported by the owner: onset, duration and progression, appetite, thirst, vomiting/diarrhoea, urination/defecation, energy, cough/sneezing, pruritus, lameness, diet, preventive care, current medications and supplements, relevant past history, travel/exposure. Attribute statements to the owner. Do not include clinician findings here.</instructions>
</section>
<section id="vitals" title="Objective - Vitals" format="key_value" required="true" missing_behavior="state_not_discussed">
<instructions>Record the vital signs and measurements exactly as stated. Leave a field blank if it was not measured or mentioned; never estimate a value.</instructions>
<field key="temperature" label="T" hint="Rectal temperature with unit (F or C)"/>
<field key="heart_rate" label="HR" hint="bpm; include rhythm/murmur grade only if stated"/>
<field key="resp_rate" label="RR" hint="breaths/min; note effort or panting if stated"/>
<field key="weight" label="Weight" hint="kg or lb exactly as stated; include change from last visit if stated"/>
<field key="bcs" label="BCS" hint="Body condition score, e.g. 5/9"/>
<field key="mm" label="MM" hint="Mucous membrane colour/moisture"/>
<field key="crt" label="CRT" hint="Capillary refill time in seconds"/>
<field key="pain_score" label="Pain score" hint="Pain score and scale used, if stated"/>
</section>
<section id="physical_exam" title="Physical Exam" format="paragraph" required="true" missing_behavior="use_normal_defaults">
<instructions>Physical examination by body system as stated by the clinician: general appearance/attitude, hydration, eyes/ears/nose/throat, oral cavity, lymph nodes, cardiovascular, respiratory, abdomen/GI, urogenital, musculoskeletal, integument, neurologic. Document every abnormal finding exactly as described, with location and severity. Systems the clinician did not mention are filled from the normal defaults and flagged for confirmation.</instructions>
<normal_defaults>BAR. Well hydrated. MM pink and moist, CRT <2 s. Eyes, ears and nose clear/clean, no discharge. Oral cavity: no gross abnormalities. Peripheral lymph nodes normal size. Heart: regular rhythm, no murmur or arrhythmia ausculted. Lungs: clear bilaterally, normal bronchovesicular sounds, no cough elicited. Abdomen: soft, non-painful, no masses or organomegaly palpated. Musculoskeletal: ambulatory x4, no lameness, joints normal. Skin and coat: no lesions or ectoparasites noted. Neuro: appropriate mentation, no deficits noted. Urogenital: no abnormalities noted.</normal_defaults>
</section>
<section id="assessment" title="Assessment" format="bullets" required="true" missing_behavior="state_not_discussed">
<instructions>Problem list with the clinician's diagnoses or differentials, in order of clinical priority. Keep the clinician's certainty level (suspect / likely / confirmed). Include a brief rationale only if the clinician gave one.</instructions>
</section>
<section id="plan" title="Plan" format="bullets" required="true" missing_behavior="state_not_discussed">
<instructions>Diagnostics performed or recommended (and whether accepted/declined), treatments given in clinic, medications dispensed or prescribed (drug, dose, route, frequency, duration - only if stated), diet/management advice, client communication and consent, and follow-up/recheck timing.</instructions>
</section>
</template>

<name>Biscuit</name>
<species>canine</species>
<breed>Labrador Retriever</breed>
</patient>

<section id="visit_summary" title="Why You Visited Today" format="paragraph" required="true" missing_behavior="state_not_discussed">
<instructions>A short plain-language explanation of why the pet came in and what the veterinary team found, avoiding jargon.</instructions>

<instructions>The diagnosis or most likely cause(s) explained simply, honestly reflecting any uncertainty the veterinarian expressed.</instructions>

</section>

<instructions>Warning signs the veterinarian told the owner to watch for, and when to seek emergency care.</instructions>
</section>
<section id="next_steps" title="Next Steps" format="bullets" required="true" missing_behavior="state_not_discussed">
